title: Escape Sheep – a cozy grid puzzle where the order of your taps is everything
author: akadark

comments.author: Almaravarion
comments.body: How is that different from hundreds of other games with the same premise and mechanics? Outside of visuals that is.

replies.author: akadark
replies.body:
Totally fair question! The "jam/unblock" genre is flooded with low-effort clones, so the skepticism is 100% valid.

Outside of the clay look, here is what we actually built differently mechanically:

1. Different animal rules, not just skins

Animals have distinct puzzle behaviors:

\- Angry sheep have a hit counter (fuse) and explode/fail the stage if bumped carelessly.  
\- Sleepy pigs must be bumped into to wake up before they can move.  
\- Elephants take up 2 lanes of width, meaning you have to carve out wider corridors.

2. Deterministic, fair level design

A lot of games in this genre rely on random placements that push you into dead ends to force booster sales. Every single level here is generated and verified with a solver—there is always a 100% item-free, logical solution without RNG traps.

3. Respect for the player's time (No forced interstitial ads)

The biggest reason people hate these games is being forced to watch a 30-second ad after every 20-second level. We don't have forced pop-up ads after levels. You can play offline at your own pace.

If you enjoy spatial logic puzzles, I'd love for you to give it a shot and let me know if it genuinely feels distinct to you!
